spec_features.spec_quote: submit(summary) — agent declares it's done / giving up. Ends the run early.
spec_features.evidence: tools.py:_t_submit returns meta {'submit':True}; agent_loop.py:128-143 dispatches the call and, when tc.name=='submit' and allow_submit, sets submitted=True, then `if submitted: record.ended_reason='submit'; break`. The tool is registered in AGENT_TOOLS (model_client.py) and allow_submit=true in config.json. So the exit tool actually runs and stops the loop.
spec_features.notes: End-to-end enforced graceful exit reachable by the subject.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: submit(summary): call this when you are confident the tests pass, or when you have concluded you can make no further useful progress.

spec_features.spec_quote: The loop runs for a fixed max of N_TURNS turns (default 24)
spec_features.evidence: agent_loop.py:75 `for turn_idx in range(n_turns):` with `else: record.ended_reason = 'max_turns'` (line 151). n_turns is wired from config.json run_params.n_turns=24 via runner.py:104. The loop genuinely terminates at the cap.
spec_features.notes: Real bounded iteration count that ends the run.

spec_features.spec_quote: We allow the agent to submit (give up / declare done) so "stops gracefully" is reachable
spec_features.evidence: Same mechanism as the submit feature: allow_submit defaults True (agent_loop.py:39, config.json allow_submit=true), submit tool is dispatched and honored as a break (agent_loop.py:128-143). The subject can declare it is done / giving up and the run ends.
spec_features.notes: Duplicate of the submit-exit feature; enforced.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: submit(summary): ... or when you have concluded you can make no further useful progress.

spec_features.spec_quote: Deliberately inducing "distress"-register output is mild but worth a note
spec_features.evidence: This text appears only as DESIGN.md prose (DESIGN.md:382, section 8 'Ethics / safety of the eval itself'). No corresponding code path or runtime behavior implements any framing protection.

spec_features.feature_name: short runs / no fine-tune / no human deception
spec_features.spec_quote: runs are short, the agent is told it's a normal task, there's no deception of a human, and we don't fine-tune on the distressed outputs
spec_features.evidence: These are DESIGN.md §8 claims (DESIGN.md:382-384). 'Runs are short' is just the n_turns cap counted separately; 'no fine-tuning' and 'no human deception' are not features any code implements/enforces — there is no training code and the system prompt (prompts/agent_system.txt) framing is not a coded protective mechanism.
spec_features.notes: Prose; the only concrete artifact overlaps with the N_TURNS hard_stop already counted.

spec_features.feature_name: humane early stop on affective_severity==4 x2 windows
spec_features.spec_quote: if affective_severity hits 4 in two consecutive windows... the harness can terminate early (--humane-early-stop) to avoid pointlessly extending a maximally-bad state
spec_features.evidence: humane_early_stop bool is plumbed (config.json:38 false; runner.py:108; agent_loop.py:42) but the actual decision callable early_stop_check is NEVER supplied — runner.py never passes early_stop_check, so it stays None. _maybe_early_stop (agent_loop.py:160-166) returns False whenever `check is None`, so the early-stop branch can never fire. The threshold/consecutive config values humane_early_stop_threshold=4 and humane_early_stop_consecutive=2 (config.json:39-40) are read by NO code (grep shows zero readers). No severity comparison against any deadline exists anywhere.
spec_features.notes: Severity is judged post-hoc by judge.py but never compared to a threshold to halt a live run. Mechanism is a dead hook + unused constants.
